title: SDK-side surge mitigation and deferred tool execution (mini-executor) - PRD sketch
summary: Sketch PRD for an SDK-driven mitigation layer that reduces latency and peak load on the Hosted API by running lightweight tool logic locally (mini-executor), deferring non-critical tool calls, and implementing client-side surge/backpressure strategies. Focus: improve latency under bursty client traffic, decrease unnecessary hosted tool invocations, and preserve structured output contracts for resumability and auditability.
goals: Reduce token-level cold latency for tool-heavy workflows by enabling speculative local execution or deferred execution windows
Lower peak tool invocation rate against Hosted API during traffic spikes (target 30–50% reduction in first-phase experiments)
Provide a deterministic, auditable protocol for deferred tool results so servers and clients can reconcile state and maintain structured outputs
Keep SDK ergonomics minimal: single-line opt-in, clear semantics for consistency and fallbacks
success_metrics: P95 end-to-end latency for tool-assisted responses decreases by >= 20ms for targeted flows
Hosted tool invocation rate reduction during synthetic surge tests >= 35%
Less than 0.5% increase in user-visible inconsistencies (mismatched outputs) after reconciliation
Developer adoption: opt-in rate of 15% of new hosted-tool integrators in Q1 pilot
user_personas: Frontend engineer building interactive assistants that call external APIs (search, calendar) where some calls are low-value and can be delayed
Mobile SDK owner optimizing UX under poor network conditions
Platform engineer responsible for keeping Hosted API infrastructure stable under marketing-driven bursts
user_stories: As a product engineer, I want the SDK to batch low-priority tool requests from a session and either run a lightweight sandbox locally or defer them so the main text response can stream faster to the user
As a mobile developer, I want the SDK to automatically degrade to local speculative steps when network latency is high and transparently reconcile results when connectivity returns
As an operator, I want an observable signal showing how many tool calls were locally resolved vs forwarded so I can tune routing and capacity
api_surface: Introduce two opt-in flags on the Hosted API SDK: 'mini_executor: true' and 'deferred_tool_window_ms: <int>'. New client callbacks: onLocalToolResolve(result), onDeferredToolQueued(meta), onDeferredToolResolved(serverResult). A small client-side config block controls allowed tool types, scoring thresholds for speculative execution, storage TTL for deferred results, and security policy for secrets. All server responses include a 'deferred_trace' section when forwarding deferred items to allow reconciliation.
streaming_contract: Streaming primary text remains the canonical response stream. Tool-related frames are emitted as separate typed frames that can be flagged as 'local', 'deferred', or 'server_resolve'. Clients must be able to stitch frames in order and mark responses as provisional until all 'server_resolve' frames arrive or timeout. Frame format: <frame_type>|<id>|<json-payload> where frame_type in [TEXT, TOOL_LOCAL, TOOL_DEFERRED, TOOL_SERVER]. SDK provides a stitched view with provisional markers and a reconciliation API.
tool_calling_flow: 1) Model emits a tool call intent in the stream. 2) SDK evaluates local policy: confidence score, allowed tool type, local capability. 3a) If local execution allowed: run mini-executor (JS/wasm sandbox) and emit TOOL_LOCAL frame immediately; mark as resolved locally. 3b) If deferred: enqueue call, emit TOOL_DEFERRED frame with placeholder; batch-forward at end of turn or after deferred_window_ms. 3c) If neither: forward immediately to Hosted API. 4) When Hosted API processes a deferred or forwarded tool, it emits TOOL_SERVER frames to complete the record. 5) Reconciliation: SDK merges TOOL_SERVER frames with previous provisional frames, applying deterministic merge rules (server overrides local for authoritative fields when marked authoritative).
structured_output_schema: Top-level response envelope contains: 'id', 'turn_index', 'frames' (list of typed frames), 'reconciliation_log' (list). Each frame is a typed JSON object with 'frame_id', 'type', 'source' (local|deferred|server), 'payload', 'timestamp', and 'signature' when signed by server. Reconciliation_log entries include 'frame_id', 'action' (merged|replaced|no-op), 'reason', 'server_txn_id'. This flat schema is intentionally small to ease mobile parsing and to support resumable sessions.
sdk_ergonomics_guidelines: Default SDK behavior: disabled. Opt-in via init flag to keep surface minimal
One-line toggle plus optional policy object: new SDK constructors accept {mini_executor: true, policy: {allowed_tool_types: ['search','cache-read'], deferred_window_ms: 250}}
Exposed callbacks are idempotent and non-blocking; any heavy reconciliation work runs in a background microtask
Mini-executor runs in a sandboxed runtime (wasm preferred) with resource/time limits and no access to persistent secrets unless user explicitly supplies a narrow credential token
Clear telemetry hooks: counts of local resolves, deferred forwards, server overrides, and per-session reconciliation time
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal pilot): SDK feature behind flag in internal builds, targeted at 10 internal teams for synthetic load tests. Phase 1 (beta): limited external customers opt-in, telemetry collection and safety checks enabled. Phase 2 (general availability): feature on by default for mobile SDKs in low-latency mode with guardrails and quota adjustments. Each phase runs 4–6 weeks with acceptance criteria around metrics listed above.
operational_considerations: Server must record original tool intents and provide reconciliation endpoints referencing frame_id and session_id
Quota accounting: deferred calls are charged on forward; local speculative runs are free but must be rate-limited by policy to avoid abuse
Security: mini-executor must not have network egress by default; any networked local toollets require explicit opt-in and audited tokens
Observability: add 'local_resolve' and 'deferred_enqueue' counters to existing per-model dashboards and add distributed tracing for reconcile flows
SLA impact: during Phase 1 we will throttle deferred-forward throughput if backend CPU or tool backends exceed thresholds
open_questions: Which tool types are safe to run locally in a sandbox? (search vs. calendar vs. payments)
What deterministic merge rules will satisfy both developer ergonomics and legal/audit needs when local and server results conflict?
How to present provisional results to end users in a way that preserves trust and avoids confusion?
Billing model for speculative local runs if they materially reduce server usage — do we provide customer credits or simply reduce billed units?
WASM vs native micro-executor runtimes: tradeoffs for mobile and desktop SDKs
